the adenosine contributes to the reflex responses induced by activation of TRPV1 receptors in the muscle afferent nerves and the adenosine is likely to impair TRPV1 response under the diseased conditions in which the levels of adnosine are elevated in the hindlimbs.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of adeno-sine in the regulation of muscle afferent reflex sympathetic and presser responses evoked by activation of TRPV1.
the role of adrenergic receptors (AR) and TRPV1 in the regulation of blood pressure (BP).
the mechanisms of reflex control of RSNA and BP
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adenosine is an inhibitory neuromodulator for TRPV1-evoked afferent nerve reflex responses in the hindlimbs of rats.
adenosine plays an inhibitory role in modulating the muscle afferent capsaicin-evoked reflex sympathetic and presser responses.
adenosine plays an important role in the regulation of the reflex RSNA response to TRPV1 activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adenosine is a modulator of the TRPV1-mediated reflex response.
adenosine is a novel regulator of muscle afferent reflex responses evoked by capsaicino.
adenosine may be an endogenous modulator of muscle afferent activity and may contribute to the pathophysiology of cardiovascular diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TRPV1-mediated afferent nerve activity is attenuated by adenosine, and this effect is likely to be mediated by the A2A subtype of adenosine receptor in muscle afferents.
adenosine is an endogenous modulator of the muscle afferent reflex responses evoked by activation of TRPV1.
adenosine is an important neuromodulator of muscle sensory nerve activity.
